w05:4: This week's map — from the birth of a universe, through its parents, the spirits that tend the mind, and the local universe Sons, to our unseen friends the angels
w05:7: Part Two turns our gaze from the center of the universe to our own neighborhood. The Urantia Book pictures Nebadon, the local universe we live in, as a home that the Creator Son Michael and the Universe Mother Spirit prepared over more than a billion years and built together. In this home the Universal Father rules through His Son, while the Mother Spirit tends our minds through the seven adjutant mind-spirits and the Holy Spirit. Sons such as the Melchizedeks and the Life Carriers, together with the seraphic angels, form one family that helps mortals grow. This week we meet the shape of this home and the members of its household, one by one.
w05:12: Months before a baby is born, the parents get a room ready. They paint the walls, bring in a little crib, and hang curtains. The baby opens its eyes there knowing nothing of how the room was prepared, and only much later, grown up, understands the waiting that went into it.
w05:14: The story told in Part Two of The Urantia Book is much like this. Over the past three weeks we looked at the big picture: Paradise, Havona, and the seven superuniverses. Now, within that picture, we come back to the home where we were born. This home has a name, Nebadon. It has a builder, and it has a household.
w05:16: Many unfamiliar names will appear, but there is no need to memorize them. It is enough to sense who built this home and who looks after us here.
w05:20: A hundred constellations, ten thousand systems
w05:22: In Week 3 we traced our cosmic address from a planet up to a superuniverse. In that address, the "local universe" is the unit that one Creator Son builds and governs. Paper 32 gives its size in its very first sentence.
w05:26: One hundred times one hundred times one thousand: the goal is ten million inhabited worlds. Nebadon is a young universe, not yet halfway there.
w05:30: Our system, Satania, has 619 inhabited worlds, and Urantia is one of them.
w05:34: The building begins long before the Creator Son arrives. The Paradise force organizers set nebulae in motion, and the power directors of the superuniverse gather that energy and shape it into suns and planets.
w05:38: The ground is laid first. Only when it is ready does the owner of the house arrive.
w05:42: The "Creative Daughter of the Infinite Spirit" is the one who later becomes the Universe Mother Spirit. The first work of these two was to build the capital, Salvington.
w05:46: Next come a hundred constellation headquarters and ten thousand system headquarters; Sons and angels are brought into being, and a government is set up. Human beings come at the very end of this long sequence.
w05:50: How a universe is born — from energy to mortal man (the author's summary of 32:1–2)
w05:52: Why not build it perfect from the start?
w05:54: Havona was perfect from the beginning, but a local universe becomes perfect gradually, by evolving. Why such a long road?
w05:58: Starting at the very bottom is called good fortune. Only someone who has climbed a staircase all the way knows each step. Our clumsy beginning is part of the plan.
w05:63: **Nebadon**: The name of the local universe we belong to; a young universe growing toward a goal of ten million inhabited worlds.
w05:64: **Salvington**: The capital of Nebadon, an architectural sphere where Michael and the Mother Spirit have their headquarters.
w05:65: **Power directors**: Superuniverse beings who gather the energies of space and shape them into suns and planets.
w05:66: **Constellations and systems**: The administrative divisions of a local universe. Each constellation holds a hundred systems, and each system about a thousand inhabited worlds.
w05:69: 2. Michael the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit
w05:73: Who is the master of this great house? Paper 32 gives a remarkable name.
w05:77: The Creator who made our universe came to this planet and lived as a man. He is Jesus of Nazareth (Week 11). What is Michael to us?
w05:81: The phrase "to all practical intents and purposes" deserves attention. Paper 33 states plainly that Michael is neither the Eternal Son of Paradise nor a member of the Trinity (33:1.2). The point is that every aspect of God that we are able to recognize is gathered up in him.
w05:83: The Father works through the Son
w05:85: Where, then, is the Universal Father? The opening paragraph of Paper 33 sets out the principle of local universe administration.
w05:89: The Father hands over this work out of generosity, not indifference. Paper 32 says, "God is not a self-centered personality" (32:4.10). Nor does handing it over mean He stands at a distance.
w05:93: And the Father does not work only through His Son. Within each person He is present Himself.
w05:98: Jesus told Philip, "he that hath seen me hath seen the Father" (John 14:9). After the resurrection he declared, "All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth" (Matthew 28:18). The Urantia Book reads both sayings from the standpoint of the Creator Son. The Father is present in the Son (32:3.6), and only after the Mother Spirit pledged her subordination to Michael was "all power in heaven and on earth" committed to his hand (33:3.5).
w05:103: At Michael's side stands a companion, who chose this path freely from the start.
w05:107: The Mother Spirit is also called the Divine Minister. When Michael returned after finishing his final bestowal on this world, she acknowledged the Son as sovereign. Michael in turn raised her to be his coruler.
w05:111: The way these two honor each other is the model for every family.
w05:115: Our universe is not a government office but a home where parents watch over their children.
w05:118: **A common misunderstanding**: Since God has handed the local universe over to His Son, the Universal Father must be resting somewhere far away from us.
w05:119: **What The Urantia Book says**: We should not think of the Father as silent or inactive (32:4.1). In person He rules through His Son, yet in the minds of His mortal children He is truly present as the indwelling Adjuster (32:3.4, 32:4.5). He delegates the administration, yet He is closest of all to each individual.
w05:122: 3. The Spirits That Tend the Mind
w05:126: The Mother Spirit takes special care of mind. Paper 34 says that three spirit circuits flow through our universe.
w05:130: The Spirit of Truth comes from Michael the Son; the Holy Spirit and the seven adjutant mind-spirits come from the Mother Spirit. In this book, "Holy Spirit" means the spiritual presence of the local universe Mother Spirit.
w05:134: Working at the lowest level are the seven adjutant mind-spirits.
w05:138: What the seven adjutant mind-spirits do (the author's summary of 36:5.6–12)
w05:141: Quick perception; the instinct of self-preservation
Pulling a hand back from something hot
w05:142: Sizing up a situation and deciding at once
w05:143: Loyalty; the root of moral stamina
Doing the right thing despite fear
w05:144: Curiosity and discovery; the scientific spirit
Following a question through to the end
w05:145: The social urge; the ability to work together
Talking things over and cooperating with neighbors
w05:146: The religious urge; the badge of a soul candidate
Bowing before One greater than oneself
w05:147: Coordinates the work of all the adjutants
Drawing on past experience to find the right way
w05:149: These spirits are at work from the most primitive life onward.
w05:155: The first five spirits act on animals too. What makes a human being human is the sixth and the seventh. Paper 36 introduces the spirit of worship this way.
w05:159: Long ago someone knelt for the first time before something greater than himself. Paper 34 explains what happened at that moment.
w05:163: The moment a mind turns toward worship, the ministry of the Holy Spirit begins. Such a person can then receive an Adjuster, and once the Spirit of Truth has been poured out, every normal mind receives one (34:5.4).
w05:167: Layers of mind — from the adjutant mind-spirits to the Holy Spirit, the Spirit of Truth, and the Adjuster (the author's summary of 34:4–5 and 36:5)
w05:171: Yet two forces are always contending within us. Paper 34 does not hide this fact.
w05:175: When heart and conduct pull in different directions, that is not a private failure but the condition of us all. Alongside us, the Spirit simply leads.
w05:179: Near the end of Paper 42 one sentence captures this relationship in a single picture.
w05:183: The body in the mirror is not the whole of a person. To those who have set out on this road, Paper 34 makes a promise.
w05:188: **Universe Mother Spirit (Divine Minister)**: The daughter of the Infinite Spirit who creates and governs Nebadon together with Michael.
w05:189: **Seven adjutant mind-spirits**: Seven circuits through which the Mother Spirit works at the level of mind, helping its basic capacities from intuition to wisdom.
w05:190: **Holy Spirit**: In this book, the spiritual presence of the local universe Mother Spirit.
w05:194: The Book of Revelation speaks of "seven lamps of fire burning before the throne, which are the seven Spirits of God" (Revelation 4:5). Paper 34 explains this as a vision of the seven adjutant mind-spirits (34:4.11). It also quotes Paul's "fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance" (Galatians 5:22–23) as the mark of a spirit-led life (34:6.13).
w05:197: 4. The Sons of the Local Universe
w05:199: Gabriel and the frame of government
w05:201: The first being that Michael and the Mother Spirit created together is the Bright and Morning Star, Gabriel of Salvington. There is only one such being in each local universe, and he carries out the actual administration.
w05:205: Beneath him govern the Constellation Fathers, the System Sovereigns, and the Planetary Princes. Immanuel of Salvington, ambassador of the Paradise Trinity, gives counsel only when asked (33:5.2). Michael gives himself to creation, sustenance, and ministry alone, and takes no personal part in judging (33:7.1).
w05:209: How Nebadon is governed — from the universe parents down to a planet (the author's summary of Papers 33 and 35)
w05:213: After Gabriel, Michael and the Mother Spirit brought forth many orders of Sons. Paper 35 introduces four of them.
w05:217: Four orders of local universe Sons (the author's summary of Papers 35–36)
w05:220: Eldest sons of the family; emergency Sons
Lead the schools; hurry to help in crises
Melchizedek of Salem, the third revelation
w05:222: The rebellion of Lucifer and Caligastia
w05:223: Planted life in the primitive seas
w05:227: The Melchizedeks are the first order of Sons able to stand midway between heaven and earth and serve the evolutionary races directly. Paper 35 likens them to the eldest child in a household.
w05:231: Here is the picture of an eldest child who looks after the younger ones unasked. Their main work is teaching ascenders, but they have another name as well.
w05:235: Melchizedek of Salem, whom we met in Week 1, was a Son of this order who came in human likeness in a time of crisis (35:4.5).
w05:239: The Lanonandeks are the Sons who govern systems and planets. Coming closest to human beings brings the greatest risk.
w05:243: Lucifer, once the sovereign of our system, and Caligastia, once the prince of our planet, both belonged to this order. The story of their rebellion comes in Week 7.
w05:247: The fourth order, the Life Carriers, answers an old question about the origin of life.
w05:251: Like a gardener who stays beside the seeds he has sown, the Life Carriers remain long after planting life to foster its growth (36:0.1). The story of life on Urantia continues in Week 8.
w05:254: **Bright and Morning Star**: The first being created jointly by the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit, the chief executive of a local universe; in Nebadon, Gabriel of Salvington.
w05:255: **Melchizedek Sons**: The eldest-son order of the local universe; they lead the education of ascenders and step in as "emergency Sons" on worlds in crisis.
w05:256: **Vorondadek and Lanonandek Sons**: Local universe Sons who govern constellations (Vorondadeks) and systems and planets (Lanonandeks).
w05:257: **Life Carriers**: Sons who design life, plant it on planets, and tend its development.
w05:264: While Michael was bringing forth Sons, the Mother Spirit by herself created the angels. The angels who help mortals most closely in a local universe are the seraphim. Paper 38 describes them this way.
w05:268: They are far closer than the winged angels of paintings. They are friends who enjoy even our songs and our jokes, and the friendship grows deeper after death.
w05:274: Among the seraphim, experienced angels are assigned to one person and walk with that person for a lifetime. They are called guardians of destiny.
w05:278: In guarding us, a guardian angel is also walking toward its own destiny. Paper 113 says, "The teaching about guardian angels is not a myth" (113:1.1). We will return to them in a later week.
w05:280: A bridge between matter and spirit
w05:282: Between humans and angels there are still other members of the household: the midwayers, who stand between humans and angels, and the cherubim, the lowest of the angels. Paper 38 says that together they link the material and spiritual worlds without a gap.
w05:286: A bridge between matter and spirit — the ladder of care from human beings to the seraphim (the author's summary of 38:9.9)
w05:288: The first link in a long chain
w05:290: The seraphim of Paper 39 known as the quickeners of morality picture mortal life as an unbroken chain.
w05:294: What carries on into eternity is less what we do than the spirit in which we do it. Paper 40 is honest about where mortals stand among the ascending sons.
w05:298: A being on the lowest rung, yet divinely loved and free to choose the highest destiny: that is a human being. How wide is that door?
w05:302: A single faint flicker is enough. This home, prepared over more than a billion years, has been waiting for children who carry that small light. Next week we enter the mansion worlds, where we awaken after death.
w05:305: **A common misunderstanding**: Angels watch from on high to accuse people of their faults, so we should pray to them and worship them.
w05:306: **What The Urantia Book says**: Angels are above us in spiritual status, but they are not our judges or accusers (38:2.4). It is good to love them, but they must not be worshiped; the angels themselves say each is a "fellow servant" who also worships God (38:2.5). Angels are friends who understand our struggles and cheer us on.
w05:310: A local universe is the work of one Creator Son, evolving toward a hundred constellations, ten thousand systems, and ten million inhabited worlds. Ours is named Nebadon.
w05:311: After the power directors laid the foundation, Michael and the Creative Spirit spent more than a billion years building Salvington; mortal man comes at the very end.
w05:312: Michael, the sovereign of Nebadon, lived on this earth as Jesus of Nazareth. The Universal Father rules the local universe through His Son, yet is intimately present in the human mind as the Adjuster.
w05:313: Michael and the Universe Mother Spirit care for the universe like a father and a mother. The Proclamation of Equality is the pattern for every family and every government.
w05:314: The Mother Spirit tends the mind through the seven adjutant mind-spirits and the Holy Spirit. When the spirits of worship and wisdom are at work, mind crosses the threshold of spiritual ministry.
w05:315: Local universe Sons such as the Melchizedeks, Vorondadeks, Lanonandeks, and Life Carriers teach, govern, and plant life.
w05:316: The seraphim are unseen friends who understand and love human beings, and as guardians of destiny they walk each person's road alongside them. Yet they are not to be worshiped.
w05:320: How does the picture of our universe as a "home" where a father and mother watch over their children, rather than a government office (33:3.7), change the way you think about your relationship with God?
w05:321: Which of the seven adjutant mind-spirits do you feel you most need in your life right now? What might it mean that the spirits of worship and wisdom mark a "threshold" (34:5.3)?
w05:322: In light of the words "Even the work of this world … is not nearly so important as the way in which you do this work" (39:4.13), how might you do today's ordinary tasks differently?

w06:1: Beyond Death, into the School of the Universe
w06:2: Papers 47–48 · Paper 112:3–7 · Paper 30:4 · Paper 43:8 · Paper 45:7 · Paper 46:0 · Paper 35:3
w06:3: This week's map — from death and resurrection, through the seven mansion worlds, morontia life and Adjuster fusion, to the three capitals of the local universe
w06:6: The Urantia Book pictures death not as an ending but as a doorway into the next life. After death no one becomes a perfect spirit at once; instead, a person climbs step by step through the morontia stage that lies between matter and spirit. The first steps, the seven mansion worlds, are a school where what was left unfinished on earth is supplied and set right, and where many fuse forever with the indwelling Adjuster. This week we follow the ascending path of the local universe, from the resurrection morning to Jerusem, Edentia, and Salvington.
w06:11: Families keeping watch at a bedside tend to ask the same last questions. Will this person still be the same person? Will we meet again? What happens to a life that was cut short?
w06:13: For a long time people have been offered two kinds of answer. One says that death ends everything. The other says that at the moment of death a person passes straight into eternal reward or punishment. The Urantia Book shows a third way. Death is rather like changing schools. I wake up as myself, take up learning where I stopped, and can look for those who went before me. This week we walk through that new school, from its front gate to graduation day.
w06:17: There Is No Magic in Death
w06:19: The book's teaching on life after death begins with one firm statement: death does not turn anyone into a finished being in an instant.
w06:23: "Morontia" names the in-between state that lies between matter and spirit. No one leaps from material life to spirit life in one bound. A long bridge spans the gap, and that bridge is the morontia career. Nor does the bridge suddenly appear at death. Morontia life has already begun here on earth, at the moment the Adjuster arrives and the soul is conceived (48:6.2).
w06:25: What Happens at the Moment of Death
w06:27: So when breathing stops, what goes where? Paper 112 explains that the body, the Adjuster, and the soul each take a different road.
w06:31: The body returns to dust, the Adjuster goes home for a time carrying the worthwhile record of the life, and the soul is entrusted to a guardian angel. When these three meet again, that is resurrection. And what does the sleeping soul go through? Nothing at all, the book answers.
w06:35: At the moment of death, what goes where (arranged by the author from 112:3.5 and 112:5.13)
w06:38: The elemental world, that is, the dust
w06:39: Keeps the worthwhile record of the mind
w06:40: The custody of the destiny guardian
Holds the pattern of identity, unconscious
w06:41: The uniqueness bestowed by the Father
w06:42: Returns on awakening in the mansion worlds
w06:44: At Once, or at the End of an Age
w06:46: Not everyone wakes at the same time. Those who have grown enough to receive a personal guardian angel awaken on the mansion worlds directly, at the "third period." The rest awaken as a group when an age ends and a Son of God calls the roll; they are called "sleeping survivors" (30:4.11). Is a long wait a disadvantage?
w06:50: And what if a case is uncertain? Paper 112 says that the universe government always decides in the person's favor.
w06:56: The place of awakening is the resurrection halls on the first mansion world, a vast temple for the assembly of personality.
w06:60: The one who wakes is no stranger. The very same person who lived on earth opens new eyes in a new body.
w06:64: The phrase "just where they left off" matters. Death makes no one wiser, and no one holier.
w06:68: That may sound strict, but it is really a comfort. Whatever learning and love we gather today becomes, unchanged, the starting point of the next life.
w06:70: From death to resurrection — body, Adjuster, and soul part ways and meet again in the resurrection halls (arranged by the author from 112:3.5, 30:4.11-15, 47:3.3-5)
w06:73: **Morontia**: the in-between state that lies between matter and spirit; after death a person passes through it and gradually becomes spirit.
w06:74: **Soul**: the immortal self that the human mind and the indwelling Adjuster grow together, which survives death.
w06:75: **Guardian of destiny**: the guardian angel assigned to one person, who keeps that person's soul after death.
w06:76: **Divinington**: one of the Father's worlds around Paradise, the home of the Thought Adjusters.
w06:80: **A common misunderstanding**: For a while the souls of the dead wander the earth and speak to the living, or they are born again in another body.
w06:81: **What The Urantia Book says**: Until the resurrection the soul rests wholly unconscious in the care of a guardian angel. Those who have gone on to the mansion worlds cannot send messages to loved ones, and a departed Adjuster never comes back to earth (112:3.7). Resurrection is not rebirth on earth; it is awakening on the mansion worlds.
w06:84: 2. The Stairway of the Seven Mansion Worlds
w06:86: Many Mansions in the Father's House
w06:88: The name "mansion worlds" comes from a saying of Jesus. Paper 47 explains the name in its opening lines.
w06:92: Seven "transition worlds" circle Jerusem, the capital of our local system, and seven satellites in turn circle the first of these. Those satellites are the mansion worlds.
w06:95: On his last night Jesus said, "In my Father's house are many mansions" (John 14:2, KJV). The Urantia Book reads this saying as a reference to the actual training worlds where we first stay after death (30:4.17, 47:0.1). Paul's words, "It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body" (1 Corinthians 15:44), can also be read alongside the resurrection morning, when we wake in a new form.
w06:100: The first thing given to those who awaken is not a test or a judgment, but rest and reunion.
w06:104: Here is the book's answer to the question "Will we meet again?" And when the ten days of rest are over, the mansion worlds become a school.
w06:106: The First World — Where What Is Lacking Is Supplied
w06:108: Lessons on the first mansion world are almost all remedial.
w06:112: Everyone leaves this world with some blanks left unfilled. The first mansion world does not scold anyone for them; it fills them in. Parental experience is a leading example. Those who had no chance to raise children on earth gain that experience in the homes of the Material Sons on Jerusem or in the probationary nurseries (47:1.4-6). Nor are children who died too young forgotten.
w06:116: A Little More Spiritual at Every Step
w06:118: Each person stays as long as needed, then enters the "transit sleep" and moves on to the next world, receiving a new morontia body each time (47:3.10, 47:4.4). The direction of the stairway is clear.
w06:122: Notice the word "slightly." Even in heaven, growth does not arrive all at once. On the second world conflicts of the mind are healed (47:4.8), and only on the third does forward-moving education begin.
w06:126: On the fourth world ascenders first learn a true social life in which no one pushes the self forward (47:6.3). Then on the fifth world comes a great turning point.
w06:130: When what was once done by effort begins to flow on its own, that is a sign of growth. Fusion on the sixth world is taken up in section 4. On the seventh world even the differences of one's home planet are erased.
w06:134: This is a promise that being born on Urantia, a world touched by rebellion, will not be an everlasting burden. Those who finish the seventh world set out for Jerusem together as a class (47:9.3).
w06:136: The stairway of the seven mansion worlds — on each sphere less material and slightly more spiritual (arranged by the author from 47:3-9)
w06:138: 3. Morontia Life — Companions, Teachers, and Memory
w06:142: The key to the question "Will I still be me?" is memory.
w06:146: What has value remains; what has no meaning falls away with the brain. At first the past life may seem like a faint dream, but it grows clearer over time (112:5.21). And the bonds between people are never discarded.
w06:150: A Body Whose Outside Matches the Inside
w06:152: On the mansion worlds people still eat, drink, and rest (47:4.6). No one turns into a ghost. There is, however, one great difference.
w06:156: In the morontia worlds the inner person shows plainly on the outside. The way to become beautiful there begins with tending the heart today.
w06:158: A Warm Friend: The Morontia Companion
w06:160: No one walks the mansion-world road alone. A friend is there from the very moment of awakening.
w06:164: The morontia companion is guide, interpreter, and companion on outings. Paper 48 adds a delightful remark.
w06:168: God's plan contains not only what is necessary but also joy. The ascending life is divided almost evenly between work and play (48:4.1), and laughter has an important place.
w06:172: Mansion World Teachers and the Three Schools
w06:174: The Mansion World Teachers are the cherubim and sanobim who once assisted the guardian angels here on earth. Having already shared our experience, they understand us well (48:5.9). Their schools are arranged like this.
w06:178: Knowing, feeling, and living must grow together. And in this school there are no short cuts.
w06:184: Procrastination heads the list. Homework put off on earth will still be waiting over there. One of the sayings of human philosophy used on the first mansion world to teach "mota" sums up this week's teaching exactly (48:7.1).
w06:188: Three tiers of the morontia school — the schools added on the mansion worlds, in the constellation, and at universe headquarters (arranged by the author from 48:3 and 48:5.6)
w06:191: **Morontia companions**: children of the local universe Mother Spirit, friends who welcome and guide the ascenders.
w06:192: **Mansion World Teachers**: glorified cherubim and sanobim, once helpers of the guardian angels, who now teach the ascenders.
w06:193: **Mota**: morontia wisdom, higher than human philosophy.
w06:196: 4. The Day of Oneness with the Adjuster
w06:200: The Thought Adjuster who has quietly dwelt within a person will one day become one with that person forever. This is "fusion." Fusion usually takes place on the mansion worlds or on Jerusem, though now and then it happens on earth without death, and sometimes it is delayed until the universe capital (112:7.3).
w06:204: On the day of fusion a short ceremony is held while one's companions look on.
w06:210: Fusion is not an ending but a new beginning.
w06:213: When Jesus was baptized in the Jordan, a voice from heaven said, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased" (Matthew 3:17, KJV). The Urantia Book tells us that the same words are spoken over every ascender who fuses with the Adjuster (47:8.4). The "new name written" on "a white stone" in Revelation 2:17 can likewise be read alongside the new name received after fusion.
w06:218: After fusion there is no longer any danger of losing eternal life (112:7.4).
w06:222: The human receives eternity from the Adjuster, and the Adjuster receives from the human a channel of personality. Seen from God's side, this is the fulfillment of a promise.
w06:226: Even so, the fused are still somewhat material and a little lower than the angels (47:8.6). Fusion guarantees eternity; it does not end growth. Week 10 looks at the Adjusters more deeply.
w06:229: **A common misunderstanding**: To become one with God means that the individual self disappears, like a drop of water dissolving in the sea.
w06:230: **What The Urantia Book says**: The fused being is a single personality that cannot be analyzed into parts (112:7.8), yet in all matters of personality it is the human who takes the lead, because the human was the one who first possessed personality (112:7.12). The fused one is still called an "ascending mortal" to the end. The self is not erased; I remain myself forever.
w06:237: Those who finish the seventh mansion world are sent off by their companions gathered on the sea of glass, and leave to become citizens of Jerusem, the system capital (47:9.4).
w06:241: What is commonly called "heaven" turns out to be the first major station on a long journey. There ascenders learn how to govern together.
w06:245: Edentia — Where We Learn to Live Together
w06:247: After Jerusem comes Edentia, the constellation headquarters, circled by seventy training worlds.
w06:251: Learning to live with beings unlike oneself, without irritation, is the coursework of Edentia (43:8.9). Of its gardens the author confesses this.
w06:257: After graduating from the constellation, ascenders reach Salvington, the capital of the local universe. The 490 worlds around it are called the Melchizedek University.
w06:261: Of the first station there, the Melchizedek world, Paper 35 says this.
w06:265: When the studies of Salvington are complete, the long morontia bridge has been crossed, and the ascender becomes a spirit.
w06:269: Along this road the morontia body changes 570 times in all.
w06:273: Three stations of the local universe ascent (arranged by the author from 43:8, 45:7, 35:3, 48:1.5)
w06:276: Capital of the system of Satania
Making up deficiencies, unifying personality, representative government and citizenship
w06:277: Headquarters of the constellation of Norlatiadek, 70 training worlds
Group ethics, living together with other beings
w06:278: Capital of the local universe of Nebadon, 490 worlds of the Melchizedek University
Philosophy, divinity, pure spirituality, universe administration
w06:282: Why does God not simply make people perfect at once and take them straight to Paradise?
w06:286: The universe is not a resort but a school, and at the end of the school lies service. God is raising up partners who will work alongside Him. A single day on earth is the first grade of that school.
w06:288: The ascension timetable — the seven stages of the ascending career and the stretch this week covers (arranged by the author from 30:4 and 48:1.5)

w06:292: **Edentia**: headquarters of the constellation of Norlatiadek, where on seventy training worlds ascenders learn to live together.
w06:293: **Salvington**: capital of the local universe of Nebadon, where ascenders pass through the Melchizedek University and become first-stage spirits.
w06:297: Death does not turn anyone into a perfect spirit in an instant. Between matter and spirit lies the morontia career.
w06:298: After death the body returns to dust, the Adjuster goes to Divinington, and the soul is kept by the guardian of destiny. Resurrection is the reunion of these three in the resurrection halls of the mansion worlds.
w06:299: A person starts again exactly where death left off, and can seek out and meet loved ones who went before.
w06:300: The seven mansion worlds are a school, from the first world where deficiencies are made up to the seventh where ascenders prepare for citizenship on Jerusem, growing slightly more spiritual at every step.
w06:301: Worthwhile memories and the bonds between persons do not disappear. Morontia companions and Mansion World Teachers walk the road with us.
w06:302: Many fuse with their Adjusters on the fifth or sixth mansion world, and after that the eternal career is no longer at risk.
w06:303: Through Jerusem, Edentia, and Salvington a person becomes a first-stage spirit, and the goal of this long school is not endless rest but transcendent service.
w06:307: "You begin over there right where you leave off down here" (47:3.7). What does this say about the things you are putting off today?
w06:308: The first schools of the mansion worlds are the schools of thinking, feeling, and doing. What light does this shed on balance in your life of faith?

w07:3: This week's map — from the many inhabited worlds, through the planetary ages, the Lucifer rebellion and the delay of mercy, to light and life
w07:6: The universe holds a great many worlds where people live. On a normal world the Sons of God arrive one after another, and the planet moves through a set series of ages toward the era of light and life. But about two hundred thousand years ago Lucifer, the sovereign of our system, raised a rebellion in the name of "liberty," and Urantia was thrown far out of that order. This week looks at how true liberty differs from false liberty, why God did not end the rebellion at once, and what destiny awaits every world in the end.
w07:11: A farmer who sows a field does not gather the harvest the next morning. In the meantime the weeds grow up with the wheat. An impatient hand wants to plough the whole field under at once, but a wise farmer waits until harvest, because pulling too soon would tear up the good shoots along with the bad.
w07:13: Papers 49 to 55, which we read this week, tell the story of a field as wide as the universe. The seed of life is sown on countless worlds, and in each age heavenly workers come to tend it. In our system, however, the one entrusted with the field tried to make himself its owner. That was the Lucifer rebellion.
w07:15: It is a dark story with a bright ending. The mercy hidden in waiting, and the age of light and life that every world at last attains, are where this week arrives.
w07:21: In the past weeks we followed the soul upward after death to the mansion worlds and to Jerusem, the system capital. Now we turn our eyes downward to the planets where people live. The Urantia Book calls such planets **inhabited worlds**, and our local system, Satania, contains a good number of them.
w07:25: Our earth is one of some six hundred neighboring worlds. We are not living alone in the universe. And on every one of those worlds the appearance of human beings is no accident.
w07:29: Many Kinds of Children, One Father
w07:31: The peoples of the inhabited worlds differ remarkably. Paper 49 explains that bodies are designed for their surroundings: the atmosphere, land, water and air, gravity, and temperature. There are even worlds whose people do not breathe. Yet one thing stays the same.
w07:35: The brain, too, comes in three basic designs. This passage holds up a mirror to us.
w07:39: Curious and fond of adventure, but not very practiced at worship: that is the portrait the book paints of us. Still, however much bodies and brains may differ, heaven's care is the same for all.
w07:43: The children may look different, but the Father is one. Variety is not a flaw in the universe; it is its wealth.

w07:59: 2. The Ages a Planet Passes Through
w07:61: The Order of the Seven Ages
w07:63: Just as a school has its grades, a planet has its ages. After the Life Carriers plant life and human beings appear, the Sons of God arrive in a fixed order. Each arrival opens a new age, called a **dispensation**.
w07:67: The Planetary Prince opens the way to civilization and society, and Adam and Eve, the Material Son and Daughter, lift the race in body and mind. Then it is the turn of Sons from Paradise.
w07:71: When the bestowal Son finishes his mission, the world reaches a great turning point. The Son's spirit is poured out, and from then on the spirit of God comes to dwell in every person.
w07:75: The order has its reasons. Each Son builds on the ground the one before him prepared. Biological uplift comes first, then ethical progress, then spiritual awakening. The principle we met in Week 1, that revelation is given in measures people can bear, here shapes the whole history of a planet.
w07:79: The ages a planet passes through — the normal order and what happened on Urantia (compiled by the author from 49:5.22-27 and Paper 52)
w07:83: Hold this standard timetable up against Urantia and nearly every column is off. Caligastia, the Planetary Prince, joined the rebellion, and Adam and Eve did not complete their mission. The next column is more surprising still.
w07:87: To the most troubled of planets the Creator of the universe came in person, as a man. Yet his coming did not bring peace to the earth at once.
w07:91: The wars and divisions of our world are signs that this planet was badly wounded very early in its history. That wound is the subject of the next section.

w07:105: **Dispensation**: a stretch of planetary history opened when a Son of God arrives on a world. Each new arrival begins a new dispensation.
w07:106: **Magisterial Son**: the Paradise Son, also called an Avonal, whom we met by name in Week 4. He judges the ages of a planet and sometimes comes in the flesh on a magisterial mission.
w07:107: **Bestowal Son**: a Paradise Son who bestows himself on an evolutionary world. To Urantia the Creator Son Michael came in person.
w07:111: Jesus said, "Think not that I am come to send peace on earth" (Matthew 10:34), and he spoke beforehand of "wars and rumours of wars" (Matthew 24:6). Paper 52 explains these sayings by Urantia's being out of step with the normal planetary order (52:6.1). The Prince of Peace came, yet peace is delayed, and The Urantia Book looks for the reason in the history of the planet.
w07:114: 3. The Lucifer Rebellion — A Declaration of False Liberty
w07:116: The Fall of a Brilliant Son
w07:118: Lucifer was not evil from the start. He was one of the outstanding personalities among the Lanonandek Sons created in the local universe.
w07:122: How could such a being fall? Paper 53 does not look for the cause in outside circumstances. Nothing in Satania especially invited rebellion.
w07:126: The word to notice is "self-deception." At first Lucifer believed he was doing what was right. Pride always marches behind a plausible cause. Then, at some point, he had gone too far to turn back.
w07:128: The Three Claims of the Lucifer Manifesto
w07:130: The rebellion broke out about two hundred thousand years ago as a public declaration at the annual conclave on Jerusem.
w07:138: The second concerned the government of the universe.
w07:142: The third was aimed squarely at us, the ascending mortals.
w07:146: Put in a single line, the three claims say: there is no Father, rule from above is interference, and the long training is a waste. The slogan that bound them together was self-assertion.
w07:150: Gabriel did not answer with force. He announced only that every being would be free to choose.
w07:154: How the Lucifer rebellion unfolded — from pride in the heart to the trial on Uversa (compiled by the author from Paper 53)
w07:156: The rebellion spread through the whole system. The princes of thirty-seven planets sided with Lucifer, and many angels went over. Yet one group never wavered.
w07:160: When Lanaforge, the new System Sovereign, arrived a little over two years later, this was the first news he sent to the constellation headquarters.
w07:164: Those who had received the very ascension training that Lucifer mocked as useless stood the firmest. Truth won through experience is stronger than dazzling sophistry.
w07:168: "Liberty" was written on Lucifer's banner. For that reason Paper 54 says the deepest confusion the rebellion left behind is the failure to tell true liberty from false.
w07:172: It then draws the line between them.
w07:176: False liberty begins with "the right to do as I please" and ends in dominating others. True liberty begins with governing oneself and bears fruit in serving others. What, then, exactly was Lucifer's mistake?
w07:180: To "short-circuit time" means to skip the process and grab the result, like current jumping across a short circuit. The irony is that a rebellion shouting for liberty tried to take away the real liberty of every being to share, through its own growth, in building the universe. Paper 54 settles the point in one sentence.
w07:184: True liberty and false liberty (compiled by the author from 54:1)
w07:191: Cut off from reality and duty, it destroys itself
w07:194: **Lanonandek Son**: the order of local universe Sons we met in Week 5; System Sovereigns and Planetary Princes come from this order. Lucifer, Satan and Caligastia were all Lanonandeks.
w07:195: **Lucifer manifesto**: the declaration of rebellion Lucifer issued on Jerusem, also called the Declaration of Liberty. It attacked the reality of the Father, Michael's rule, and the mortal ascension plan.
w07:196: **Gabriel**: the chief executive of the local universe of Nebadon. During the rebellion he led the loyal hosts on Michael's behalf.
w07:200: Isaiah sings, "How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning!" (Isaiah 14:12), and Revelation reports, "And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon" (Revelation 12:7). Paper 53 links these verses to the Lucifer rebellion and explains that the "war in heaven" was not a battle of swords but a contest between truth and sophistry with eternal life at stake (53:5.6-7).
w07:203: 4. Why Was It Not Stopped at Once? — The Delay of Mercy
w07:207: Almost everyone who reads this part asks the same question: if God is all-powerful, why did He not end the rebellion on its first day? The author of Paper 54 does not avoid the question. He begins by calling to mind the heart of a parent.
w07:211: He goes on to show how justice and mercy work together in time. Here the farmer of our opening story returns.
w07:215: Between seedtime and harvest — the delay of mercy and the relativity of time (compiled by the author from 54:4.6 and 54:5.13)
w07:219: First we need to see where Michael stood at the time. He had not yet completed his seventh bestowal, his life on Urantia.
w07:223: Section 5 of Paper 54 gives twelve reasons why the rebels were not taken in hand sooner. The first few read:
w07:227: The waiting was not only for the rebels. Countless beings who hesitated on the sidelines needed time to think things through and choose. Had the rebellion been crushed by force, seeds of doubt would have stayed buried in the ground.
w07:231: Another reason is that our sense of time is narrow.
w07:235: To us two hundred thousand years seem endless, but in the courts of the superuniverse they are the blink of an eye. The author adds that forty-eight reasons are taught on Uversa, and that there are probably as many more we do not know (54:5.14).
w07:239: A question still remains: why should the innocent share the cost? Paper 54 answers with the picture of a family.
w07:243: To be bound together as a family means sharing both joy and pain. But that pain has a clear limit.
w07:247: Another's wrongdoing can hurt a life, but it cannot take away anyone's eternity. And the waiting bore fruit.
w07:251: The End of the Rebellion, and the Gift of Isolation
w07:253: When did the rebellion end in principle? Paper 53 finds that moment in the temptation in the wilderness, when Jesus, the Son of Man, turned down Lucifer's proposals.
w07:257: After the rebellion Urantia became an isolated world, its circuits to other worlds cut off. Even this seeming misfortune hides a gift.
w07:261: Ascenders like these are given a special name.
w07:265: There is no better school for learning to believe without seeing. Paper 54 closes the matter of waiting in a few words.
w07:270: **Quarantine**: the measure that cut the planets involved in the rebellion off from the universe circuits. Urantia is one of them.
w07:271: **Agondonter**: the name for ascenders from isolated worlds who believed without seeing and persevered alone.
w07:272: **Gabriel vs. Lucifer**: the case pending before the superuniverse court on Uversa that deals with the final disposition of the rebel leaders.
w07:276: **Common misunderstanding**: God created evil, or at least permitted the rebellion.
w07:277: **What The Urantia Book says**: The Gods do not create evil, nor do they permit sin and rebellion (54:0.2). They have given free will, and for that freedom to be real there must also be the possibility of choosing wrongly (54:3.1). Mercy simply allows time for such choices to ripen; it never approves of evil.
w07:281: **Common misunderstanding**: The devil seizes people and forces them to sin.
w07:282: **What The Urantia Book says**: No fallen spirit has power to invade the mind of a child of God, and faith is an effective armor against sin (53:8.8). Much that is blamed on the devil comes from human tendencies (53:8.9).
w07:285: 5. Light and Life — The Destiny of a Planet
w07:289: The story of rebellion and confusion does not end in despair. The last chapter of the seven ages is a promise that no world is abandoned.
w07:293: Not even a world "cursed by sin" is left out. Urantia, too, will reach that age, even if late and by a longer road. Paper 55 does not hide the mountains still ahead of us.
w07:297: What a World of Light and Life Is Like
w07:299: On a world settled in light and life, even death changes.
w07:303: That does not make such a world a flawless heaven.
w07:307: There are still hospitals, accidents still happen, and there is still evil to be chosen or refused. Paper 55 warns more than once against mistaking such a world for heaven.
w07:311: Light and life is not an end but the threshold of a greater journey. From the planet, settlement widens through seven stages, to the system, the constellation, the local universe and beyond (55:0.4-11).
w07:313: The seven stages of light and life — settlement widening from one planet to a whole superuniverse (compiled by the author from 55:0.4-11)
w07:315: What would it be like to see such a world even once?
w07:319: A Story That Gathers into Unity
w07:321: Paper 56, the last paper of Part II, ties all this variety and all these twists together. The many worlds, the seven ages, rebellion and recovery all become one story in the one God. Paper 56 names the climax of that story with the word beauty.
w07:325: The farmer waits because he trusts in the day of harvest. The winding history of our planet is moving toward that harvest too. Beginning next week we enter Part III and follow the story of this very planet, Urantia, from the beginning.
w07:328: Satania has 619 inhabited worlds, and Urantia is the 606th. Bodies and brains differ from world to world, but heaven's care is the same.
w07:329: A normal world passes through seven ages as the Planetary Prince, Adam and Eve, a Magisterial Son, a bestowal Son and the Teacher Sons arrive in turn.
w07:330: Urantia fell out of order through the Planetary Prince's rebellion and Adam's default, yet it was honored by the Creator Michael's coming in person as a man.
w07:331: The Lucifer rebellion grew out of pride that had reached self-deception, and it denied the reality of the Father, the rule of Michael and the ascension plan.
w07:332: True liberty is the fruit of self-control and leads to service; false liberty starts from self-assertion and exploits others.
w07:333: The rebellion was not ended at once because mercy gives every being time to choose, and its hardships can take away no one's eternal future.
w07:334: Every world at last reaches light and life, and that is not an end but the threshold of a greater ascent.
w07:338: Measured by 54:1.6, is what you call "freedom" these days the fruit of self-control or the assumption of self-assertion?
w07:339: How does the idea that waiting is mercy (54:4.6) shed light on the way you face slow change in your own life or the wrongs of others?
w07:340: Why might believing without seeing on an isolated planet (50:7.2) be an opportunity rather than a misfortune?

w08:4: This week's map — from the birth of the planet through the planting of life, the first humans and the six colored races, to the light and shadow of Dalamatia
w08:7: Part Three is the story of our own planet, Urantia. The Life Carriers waited for the world to ripen and then planted life in its seas, and that life climbed the long stair of purposeful evolution until, about a million years ago, it reached the first human beings, Andon and Fonta. About half a million years ago the six colored races were born into a single family, and around the same time the Planetary Prince, Caligastia, arrived and founded the first school for mankind at Dalamatia. The Prince joined the rebellion, but Van and Amadon held fast to the end. This week we leaf through the oldest album of our family home.
w08:12: Anyone who has stood before a road cut on a mountain highway has seen the layers: red earth, gray sand, black gravel, stacked one upon another like a layer cake. The bottom layer is the oldest, and each layer above it comes nearer to our own time. Seen from the side, the cut looks a little like a book on a shelf. Only this book is made of stone, and each page took thousands of years to lay down.
w08:14: Part Three of The Urantia Book invites us to read this book of stone together. For seven weeks we have traveled outward from Paradise, through the superuniverse and the local universe. Now, at the end of that long road, we open the door of our own home. And this home is no lump of rock that happened by chance; it was prepared through long waiting and the care of many hands.
w08:16: 1. The Birth of Urantia — From a Gas Cloud to the First Ocean
w08:20: Paper 57 begins five billion years ago with a young sun burning alone in space. Then a huge visitor drew near.
w08:28: The book calls the solar system born this way Monmatia. Here it helps to recall a principle from Week 1: cosmology of this kind organizes the scientific knowledge of its day and is subject to revision (101:4.2). What we hold on to is not the numbers but the larger thread: this home was built according to a plan.
w08:34: As the crust cooled, water vapor poured down as rain.
w08:38: At first the earth was a world of water from pole to pole. Later a single great continent rose, and when it broke apart and drifted, the sea reached into it like fingers, forming shallow, warm bays.
w08:46: These five eras roughly match the geologists' Archeozoic, Proterozoic, Paleozoic, Mesozoic, and Cenozoic. Drawn as a bar, the mammalian era in which human beings appeared is only a short segment at the very end.

w08:62: **Angona**: A huge system of bodies that passed near our sun about 4.5 billion years ago and drew out the material of the planets.
w08:63: **Monmatia**: The name of our sun and its family of planets, that is, the solar system.
w08:64: **Life-modification world**: A planet on which experiments in changing and improving the standard life designs are permitted. Urantia is such a world.
w08:67: 2. Those Who Planted Life — The Life Carriers and the Care of Evolution
w08:71: The Life Carriers, whom we met in Week 5, first came to Urantia six hundred million years ago to study conditions. Yet they did not plant life right away.
w08:77: Even celestial beings do not rush the season. They are like a farmer holding seed and waiting for the ground to thaw.
w08:81: Fifty million years later the day came.
w08:85: The authors also clear up a misunderstanding that their name might invite.
w08:89: That first sea still flows within us.
w08:95: The Urantia Book does not ask us to choose between evolution and creation. New species appear suddenly rather than through the slow piling up of small variations, and the process is entirely natural.
w08:101: At the same time, the whole process unfolds under watchful care.
w08:105: The Life Carriers are like gardeners. They do not shape the petals by hand, but they cut channels for water, shade the young plants from too much sun, and help them grow. And even their hands had limits.
w08:109: This care also has an end. Once beings appear who can choose for themselves, the Life Carriers step back, and what follows is entrusted to human hands.
w08:113: These words are both weighty and glorious. God does not keep His children forever as infants who only receive care. The wise tending of body, mind, and society now rests in human hands, and to be entrusted with something is also to be trusted.
w08:116: **A common misunderstanding**: Accepting evolution leaves no room for God, and believing in God means rejecting evolution.
w08:117: **What The Urantia Book says**: The appearance of new species is wholly natural (58:6.4), yet evolution is always purposeful, because the Life Carriers, the physical controllers, and the adjutant spirits guide it together (65:0.7). The methods of nature and the care of heaven are not at odds.
w08:120: 3. The First Humans, Andon and Fonta
w08:124: In the age when glaciers covered the land, three sudden leaps took place among the descendants of the lemur type: the dawn mammals, the mid-mammals, and the Primates.
w08:128: Here the relationship between humans and apes also becomes clear.
w08:132: The stairway to man — sudden leaps and the order of the seven adjutant mind-spirits (arranged by the author from 62:4 and 62:6)
w08:136: What made the first two humans truly human was not so much their bodies as their minds.
w08:140: The seven adjutant mind-spirits we met in Week 5 are ministers of mind sent by the Mother Spirit. The Life Carriers watched them come into play one after another. The spirits of intuition, understanding, courage, knowledge, and counsel each reached the animal brain in turn, and the two highest spirits worked for the first time in these twins. On the stairway of mind, too, it was the last two steps that set human beings apart from animals.
w08:144: On the third day after the twins left home, the first message arrived from Salvington.
w08:150: A single decision, made by thought rather than by instinct, sent a signal to heaven. Being human begins with choosing.
w08:154: The archangels named the pair Andon and Fonta, meaning the first Fatherlike and the first Sonlike creatures "to exhibit human perfection hunger" (63:0.3).
w08:158: On the journey north, Andon noticed the spark that leaps from a flint.
w08:162: As their descendants scattered, they slowly slipped backward. Then a teacher arose.
w08:168: Facing hunger, cold, and wild beasts, they still longed for the Great Beyond. And that longing was not in vain.
w08:173: **Dawn mammals, mid-mammals, Primates**: The direct animal ancestors of man, who appeared one after another by sudden leaps from the lemur type.
w08:174: **Andon and Fonta**: The first human twins, born to the Primates about a million years ago; the actual parents of all mankind.
w08:175: **Andonites**: The primitive race made up of the descendants of Andon and Fonta.
w08:176: **Onagar**: The teacher who brought peace to the declining Andonites and led them to worship the one Breath Giver.
w08:180: **A common misunderstanding**: If we speak of evolution, we mean that human beings are descended from monkeys.
w08:181: **What The Urantia Book says**: Humans and apes are only distant cousins who branched off from the same group of mid-mammals; they did not come from the same parents (62:3.12-13).
w08:184: 4. Brothers and Sisters of Six Colors — The Sangik Races
w08:186: Six Races Born into One Family
w08:188: For about half a million years after Andon and Fonta, mankind went through repeated wars and decline. Then something remarkable happened among the Badonan tribes in the highlands of northwestern India.

w08:208: How to Read the Differences of Color
w08:210: Paper 64 contains words such as "superior" and "inferior" that may make today's reader uneasy. They compare the cultural progress of groups in primitive times, and the book's scientific statements stand within the limits of the knowledge of their day. On spiritual worth, however, the book draws a clear line.
w08:214: More important still, all the colored races are children of one set of parents. The Life Carriers count this among the unique features of our planet.
w08:219: **A common misunderstanding**: The Urantia Book teaches that some races rank higher than others spiritually.
w08:220: **What The Urantia Book says**: All races have the same standing before the celestial powers (64:6.27), and the six races came from one family (65:4.7). Descriptions of cultural differences in primitive times should not be read as a spiritual judgment on people today.
w08:224: Paul said that God "hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth" (Acts 17:26, KJV). The Urantia Book shows this as history: every human being descends from Andon and Fonta, and the six colored races were born into one Sangik family.
w08:227: 5. Dalamatia and the Betrayal of Caligastia
w08:231: Around the time the Sangik races appeared, the Planetary Prince we met in Week 7 arrived on Urantia.
w08:235: This headquarters city was Dalamatia. With the Prince came a corporeal staff known as the one hundred.
w08:239: They formed ten councils of ten members each, teaching about food, animals, education, industry, religion, health, the arts, and tribal relations. Fad created the first alphabet, and Hap gave the seven commandments known as "the Father's way." Yet their greatest teaching was their own way of life.
w08:243: Civilization is the widening of love's horizon. The spirit that plants trees for generations not yet born was Dalamatia's gift.
w08:245: The Fall of a Brilliant Prince
w08:247: Peace lasted for about three hundred thousand years. Caligastia was an experienced and brilliant leader. The author, who watched him depart for his new post, makes this confession.
w08:251: When Lucifer proclaimed his rebellion, Caligastia declared himself absolute sovereign of Urantia and demanded that the ten councils surrender all their powers (67:2.1). At that moment one person stood up.
w08:255: Soon the system circuits were cut and Urantia was isolated. Even angels and midwayers each had to choose between Lucifer's way and the Father's will.
w08:259: The ten councils of the one hundred and the parting of ways after the rebellion — forty remained loyal (arranged by the author from 66:5 and 67:4.1)
w08:263: Paper 67 explains why Van never wavered.
w08:267: At Van's side stood Amadon, a man of Andonite stock.
w08:271: He was neither a superhuman visitor from on high nor an angel, but an ordinary member of the evolutionary races. The book sets him side by side with the brilliant Prince.
w08:275: Intelligence and experience do not guarantee loyalty. What keeps a person steady in the face of dazzling arguments is a straightforward devotion to the Father's will. For those seven years the eyes of the universe were fixed on one man.
w08:281: Of the one hundred, forty remained loyal; the sixty who joined the rebellion followed Nod northward, and their descendants became the Nodites (67:4.2). "Liberty" taught too soon turned into license, and in the end Dalamatia sank beneath the sea (67:5.4). Does this mean that all of us born afterward are simply victims of the rebellion?
w08:287: Van and Amadon's band withdrew to the highlands and became the leaven that lit up the long dark ages (67:6.3). From Paper 68 onward, the story continues as mankind rebuilds civilization from this low point.
w08:292: **Sangik races**: The six colored races, born about half a million years ago into a single family of the Badonan tribes.
w08:293: **Dalamatia**: The headquarters city Caligastia founded in Mesopotamia; mankind's first school.
w08:294: **The one hundred (corporeal staff)**: One hundred ascendant citizens of Jerusem who came with the Prince, took on material bodies, and taught mankind.
w08:295: **Van and Amadon**: Van was the chairman of the supreme council who refused to join the rebellion; Amadon was the Andonite who stood with him to the end.
w08:296: **Nodites**: The descendants of the sixty staff members who joined the rebellion.
w08:300: Genesis says that Cain "dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden" (Genesis 4:16, KJV), and that "the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men" (Genesis 6:4). The Urantia Book calls the region where the rebel staff's descendants lived "the land of Nod," and explains that the mating of the superhuman staff with mortals gave rise to legends of gods coming down to marry human beings (67:4.2-3).
w08:304: Urantia reached its present size about a billion years ago, and the first ocean covered the whole planet. Shallow inland seas became the cradle of evolution.
w08:305: The Life Carriers waited for the planet to ripen, then planted life in three places 550 million years ago. Urantia life is original with this planet.
w08:306: New species appear naturally, yet evolution, under heaven's care, is always purposeful.
w08:307: The first humans, Andon and Fonta, were born about a million years ago. Worship and a self-made decision marked the beginning of being human.
w08:308: About half a million years ago the six colored races were born into one Sangik family. All mankind is one family.
w08:309: Caligastia taught the first civilization at Dalamatia but joined the rebellion; Van and Amadon stayed loyal through seven years of struggle.
w08:310: The rebellion delayed civilization, but it cannot prevent the spiritual attainment of any individual who seeks God.
w08:314: The Life Carriers waited until the planet was ripe (58:1.2). What light does this shed on how you see growth and waiting in your own life?
w08:315: If what made the first humans human was the feeling of worship and a decision of their own (62:5.4, 62:7.3), what makes you human today?
w08:316: The gifted Caligastia fell, while the ordinary Amadon stood firm (67:3.9). In shaken times, where does the loyalty that holds you steady come from?

w09:1: The Lost Garden and the Way Back
w09:2: Papers 73–76 · Papers 83–84 · selections from Papers 85–92 · Paper 93
w09:3: This week's map — from the mission and default of Eden, through the long evolution of the home and of religion, to the light of Salem
w09:6: About 38,000 years ago, Adam and Eve came to Urantia to uplift the human race. Tempted by a short cut, they defaulted, yet The Urantia Book says there was no "fall of man" and that humanity was in fact lifted up. This week we follow the story of Eden, the long road along which marriage and the home have grown, the stairway by which religion climbed from fear to worship, and Melchizedek of Salem, who rekindled the truth.
w09:11: Along old mountain trails there is sometimes a weathered sign marked "Short Cut." The path looks shorter than the marked route, but stories are also told of hikers who lost their way on it. What leads people onto a short cut is usually not a bad heart but a good impatience, an eagerness to help quickly.
w09:13: The story of the Garden of Eden is familiar to many: the serpent, the forbidden fruit, the expulsion, and a curse said to have fallen on the whole human race. The Urantia Book tells this story in a very different light. At its center stands not a serpent but a short cut, and it ends not in a curse but in recovery. God's plan is greater than human failure.
w09:15: 1. The Garden of Eden and the Mission of Adam and Eve
w09:19: After the Caligastia rebellion, Urantia lay for a long time in darkness. During those years the loyal Van and Amadon preached that a promised Son of God would come, and for eighty-three years before the arrival of Adam and Eve they prepared a garden to receive him (73:2.2).
w09:23: The site chosen was a narrow peninsula reaching out from the eastern shore of the Mediterranean.
w09:27: Eden was not a golden age of myth but a real place in history. The peninsula later sank beneath the sea (73:7.1).
w09:31: And at last the two arrived.
w09:35: Adam and Eve were not the first human beings. The first humans, Andon and Fonta, were born nearly a million years ago (Week 8). Adam and Eve were a Material Son and Daughter from Jerusem, the capital of our local system. Their habit of always working together will take on great weight later in the story.
w09:39: What did they come to do? The book calls Adam and Eve "biologic uplifters." Their task was to share their own bloodline, the violet race, with the evolutionary races and so raise humanity a step higher in body and mind. But there was an order to be followed.
w09:43: First a strong violet race would be built up; only then would it go out to the whole world. The plan would take hundreds of years. The Garden was never meant to be a home to settle in, only a starting line.
w09:45: Urantia, however, was no easy world. The rebellion had cut the circuits linking the planet to the wider universe, and the deposed Caligastia was still on earth, opposing Adam's every plan (74:5.5). When the Melchizedeks who had stood beside them left after about seven years, the two were alone.
w09:49: Even a Son and Daughter from on high knew loneliness and discouragement. This honest account lets the two step out of distant legend and appear as beings with hearts much like ours.
w09:51: The course of the Eden story — from the preparation of the Garden to the second garden, the resurrection, and a new assignment (the author's summary based on Papers 73–76)
w09:54: **Material Son and Daughter**: Embodied sons and daughters of God created on the capital of a local system. One pair comes to a planet and becomes that world's "Adam and Eve."
w09:55: **Biologic uplifters**: Another name for the Material Sons and Daughters, who share their bloodline with the evolutionary races to raise humanity.
w09:56: **Violet race**: The race made up of the descendants of Adam and Eve, also called the Adamites. Blending with the Nodites and others, they later became the Andites.
w09:57: **Melchizedek receivers**: The twelve Melchizedeks who took charge of Urantia after the rebellion.
w09:60: 2. The Temptation of the Short Cut — There Was No Fall of Man
w09:64: A hundred years passed, and the world outside the Garden had changed very little. The book names the root of the trouble in a few words.
w09:68: Having failed to shake Adam, Caligastia turned to Eve. Serapatatia, a Nodite leader who had become Adam's ablest associate, put an idea before her: if a leader with some violet blood were born among the Nodites, could not the waiting tribes be helped at once? The book insists on his good faith.
w09:76: Yet the meetings grew more and more private, and a plan that ripened over more than five years finally led Eve to a meeting with Cano, a spiritual leader of the Nodites.
w09:80: The heart of the tragedy lies in the words "her own little scheme." Eve did not mean to abandon God's plan; she meant to add something to it. The aim was good, but the method left the appointed path.
w09:84: What, then, was this act? The seraphim who wrote this paper distinguish three words.
w09:90: Evil can arise from method as well as from purpose. When good intentions meet a wrong method, confusion follows. Yet that is not the same as sin. Sin is knowing God's will and deliberately setting oneself against it.
w09:92: Good, evil, and sin — distinguishing three words (the author's summary based on 75:4.3, 75:7.7, 89:10.2)
w09:96: When Adam learned what Eve had done, he went the next day to Laotta, a Nodite woman, and committed the same folly. Here the book stops the reader short.
w09:100: It was not the right choice. But beneath it ran a love that would not leave his mate alone. The two who were made to work together stayed together even as they fell.
w09:102: Gabriel's verdict was "default." The two had failed to keep the covenant entrusted to them and were reduced to mortal status (75:7.1-3). But the verdict carried an important qualification.
w09:106: There Was No Fall of Man
w09:108: For thousands of years many have believed that, because of the first man's wrongdoing, the whole human race is born under a curse. Paper 74 observes that such outlooks were discouraging because they rested on a belief in going backward rather than forward (74:8.13). Paper 75 speaks plainly.
w09:114: What fell was the standing of two persons, not the human race. From this story the author draws one warning and one comfort.
w09:120: That last sentence changes the way we see people. We are not beings who have fallen away from perfection but beings climbing toward it. Even the fact that mistakes can happen looks different in this light.
w09:126: Adam and Eve left the first garden to the Nodites, journeyed east, and founded a second garden by the Euphrates (76:0.1). There they received an unexpected gift.
w09:130: As a Material Son and Daughter they had no Thought Adjusters; once they became mortals, the Adjusters came. Where something was lost, a new road opened. Adam lived 530 years, and on the third day after his death he awoke on the mansion worlds in a special resurrection (76:6.2).
w09:134: Paper 76 gathers up their story in these words.
w09:138: It adds that this stage of failure became instead the backdrop against which a greater love would be revealed.
w09:143: **A common misunderstanding**: Through the sin of Adam and Eve the whole human race fell, and everyone inherits that sin and is born under a curse.
w09:144: **What The Urantia Book says**: By defaulting, Adam and Eve lost their own standing, but they did not commit the sin of rebellion (75:7.7). There was no "fall of man"; humanity was in fact uplifted by their contribution (75:8.1-3). Perfection is not our origin but our goal (75:8.6).
w09:148: Genesis 3 tells how God called out in the Garden, "Where art thou?" (Genesis 3:9). Paper 75 explains this scene as the memory of that night's conference between the two and the seraphic "voice in the Garden" (75:4.8). It also regards the six-day creation and the story of the rib as traditions that grew out of blended memories of the Adamic age (74:8.1-3).
w09:151: 3. Marriage and the Home — Humanity's Long Experiment
w09:155: One of the legacies Eden left behind was the ideal of the home.
w09:159: Papers 82 to 84 in Part III trace how marriage and the home evolved. On a first reading, the many unfamiliar customs, such as the buying and selling of wives and plural marriage, can be bewildering. But if we follow the main current, the direction becomes clear. Of marriage, Paper 83 says:
w09:163: The road marriage has traveled (the author's summary based on 83:0.1, 83:7, 84:7.3, 83:8.8)
w09:166: Loose unions that could end at any time
The instinctive bond of mother and child
w09:167: Wife purchase and dowry; the woman as the man's property
w09:168: Marriage motivated by love; women's rights advance
New moral codes and mutual devotion
w09:169: Faithful partnership of one man and one woman
Loyalty for the sake of rearing children
w09:171: Is marriage a divine institution or a human one? The book's answer is surprising.
w09:175: This does not belittle marriage. It means that marriage is the fruit humanity has cultivated through hundreds of thousands of years of trial and error. That fruit is not yet fully ripe, but it becomes a dream that draws humanity forward.
w09:181: Paper 84 frankly admits that men and women can never fully understand each other (84:6.3). Yet that difference is no cause for worry.
w09:189: The home is the first classroom in which people learn brotherhood.
w09:193: And Paper 84 leaves us its deepest words about the home.
w09:197: The place where a child first learns of God's love is not a book or a house of worship but the arms of its parents. Day by day, good parents show a child what the Father in heaven is like.
w09:200: **A common misunderstanding**: Marriage is a sacrament joined directly by God, and so it is a sacred union in itself.
w09:201: **What The Urantia Book says**: Marriage is man's most exalted institution, but it is essentially human, and it should never have been called a sacrament (83:8.1). At the same time, the book says that the ideal mortal marriage is "humanly sacred" (83:8.5). This does not lower marriage; it means marriage is an institution that people must take responsibility for and tend.
w09:204: 4. From Fear to Worship — The Stairway of Evolutionary Religion
w09:206: A Religion That Began in Fear
w09:208: In Week 1 we distinguished evolutionary religion from revealed religion. Papers 85 to 92 show how evolutionary religion actually grew. Its starting point was fear.
w09:212: Early humans worshiped storms and volcanoes, stones, trees, and animals. When the dead appeared in dreams, they believed ghosts had returned, and rites arose to appease them.
w09:220: All this may look foolish, but the book shows a hand at work beneath it.
w09:226: The spirit of worship brings people to their knees, and the spirit of wisdom turns those knees away from nature toward the God of nature. Even fear was not wasted.
w09:230: From fear to worship — the stairway of evolutionary religion (the author's summary based on Papers 85–91)
w09:234: Of all the burdens of evolutionary religion, sacrifice weighed on people the longest. They offered animals to appease the gods, and at times even human beings. Over the ages sacrifice met the idea of covenant and was finally transformed into a symbolic sacrament (89:8.4, 89:9.4). Summing up that long history, Paper 89 redefines sin and forgiveness.
w09:240: Forgiveness is not something bought at a price. It is a gift already in hand the moment we turn back to the Father.
w09:244: The loveliest fruit of evolutionary religion is prayer. Paper 91 draws a clear line between prayer and magic.
w09:248: Magic and true prayer (the author's summary based on 91:8.2, 91:8.7, 91:8.13)
w09:251: Bends the gods to my conditions
Brings me into line with God's will
w09:254: Attitudes change and the spirit grows
w09:260: Prayer is not a technique for changing God but the wings that lift us. How, then, does God answer prayer?
w09:264: Having surveyed this long stairway, Paper 92 urges a generous view of the world's many religions.
w09:269: **Spirit of worship, spirit of wisdom**: The sixth and seventh of the seven adjutant mind-spirits (Week 5) sent by the local universe Mother Spirit. They awaken the urge to worship and direct it toward God.
w09:270: **Cult**: A system of rites and symbols that preserves religious feeling and loyalty. It began with the ghost cult and grew all the way to the sacraments.
w09:271: **Disloyalty**: The essence of sin as Paper 89 redefines it: knowingly and deliberately turning one's back on God.
w09:274: 5. The Light of Salem: Machiventa Melchizedek
w09:278: The teachings of Eden were carried on by the Sethite priests of the second garden, but over the ages they grew ever fainter.
w09:282: At that time Machiventa, one of the twelve Melchizedeks in charge of Urantia, volunteered. Only six times in the history of Nebadon had a Melchizedek appeared on a world in human form (93:1.3). He was bestowed on this world as an "emergency Son."
w09:286: At Salem, the place later to become Jerusalem, he founded a community and a school and taught there for ninety-four years (93:2.4, 93:4.16).
w09:292: Melchizedek's teaching was utterly simple. The Salem creed had only three lines, and the second was its heart.
w09:296: Faith, not sacrifice. Recalling the long history of sacrifice in the previous section, we can see how far ahead of its time this was. That is why people found the message so hard to accept.
w09:302: Here again we see the principle from Week 1: revelation is given in the measure people can receive it.
w09:306: What Melchizedek did, and what he did not do, was clear.
w09:310: His most cherished disciple was Abraham. Abraham believed only halfheartedly, yet even that was "counted for righteousness" (93:4.5). The truth of Salem passed through Abraham, Isaac, and Joseph to Moses, and at the end of that road came Jesus.
w09:314: The ember that never went out — the relay of truth from Eden through Salem to Jesus (the author's schematic based on 92:4.6-7, 93:3, 93:9)
w09:317: Genesis 14 briefly records that "Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the most high God" (Genesis 14:18). Soon after, Abram believed in the Lord, "and he counted it to him for righteousness" (Genesis 15:6). Hebrews 7 sees Melchizedek as a type of Jesus. Paper 93 tells of the ninety-four years of ministry that lay behind these brief records.
w09:321: **Machiventa Melchizedek**: One of the twelve Melchizedeks in charge of Urantia. About four thousand years ago he appeared at Salem in human form and brought the third epochal revelation.
w09:322: **Emergency Son**: A Son bestowed specially in a crisis not provided for in the normal plan.
w09:323: **El Elyon**: A name meaning "the Most High," which Melchizedek used for the one God.
w09:326: The Garden was lost, but the road was never cut off. Next week we enter the innermost part of this long story: God who dwells within each person.
w09:329: Adam and Eve were a Material Son and Daughter who came about 38,000 years ago to uplift the human race biologically.
w09:330: Grown impatient in isolation and loneliness, Eve tried to add "her own little scheme" to the divine plan and defaulted; Adam knowingly chose to share her fate.
w09:331: Even a good motive produces evil when it uses a wrong method. Sin, however, is the knowing and deliberate transgression of God's will.
w09:332: There was no "fall of man." Perfection is not our origin but our eternal goal.
w09:333: Marriage is humanity's most exalted institution, and a good home is the first revelation of God's love.
w09:334: Religion began in fear, but under the guidance of the adjutant spirits and the Adjusters it grew into worship and prayer.
w09:335: Machiventa Melchizedek taught that God's favor is received by faith, not by sacrifice, and so prepared the way for Jesus.
w09:339: When have you tried to run ahead of God's timing with "your own little scheme"? What did you learn from it?
w09:340: How does the saying "Perfection is our eternal goal, not our origin" (75:8.6) change the way you see your own mistakes and those of others?
w09:341: How did the home you grew up in show the love of the Father in heaven? For whom are you now becoming that "first revelation" of love?
